A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeNVeR research. Their text, equations, two tables, fifteen figures, and complete supplementary material support reliable comparison. Appendices A–D in v3 correspond to supplementary Sections 6–9 in v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original XACV segmentation measurements, CADICA qualitative evaluations, component ablations, and supplementary temporal-coherence and prior-quality experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–2 and the main and supplementary figures.

M1.justification: Hessian/RAFT preprocessing, layer bootstrapping, B-spline and Eulerian motion modeling, test-time optimization, and losses remain unchanged. New analogies to canonical radiance fields and video stabilization contextualize existing components without documenting an altered procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain XACV coronary angiography data, comprising 111 videos from 59 patients, and qualitative evaluation on CADICA. The supplementary material adds no new dataset, population, domain, or test scenario relative to v3.

E2.justification: Hessian, U-Net, SSVS, DARL, and FreeCOS retain their membership in corresponding comparisons. Supplementary comparisons still include image-based and video-based U-Net. The four newly cited works are not evaluated as comparators.

E3.justification: The 8:2 training/testing split, shared thresholding and region-growing procedures, evaluation metrics, baseline training of at least 100 epochs, and supplementary five-frame supervised input are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both contain the same component ablations in Table 2 and Figure 9, loss-weight sensitivity analysis in Figure 10, temporal comparisons in Figure 14, and prior-replacement experiment in Figure 15. Renumbered supplementary sections retain the existing analyses.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same plus/minus uncertainty reporting. Run-count and seed disclosures, confidence intervals, and significance-testing practices do not change.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2, ROC/precision-recall curves, and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains DeNVeR's Dice score of 0.733±0.066, and the supplement retains the reported 2.5% Dice improvement from substituting the FreeCOS prior.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), their mathematical definitions, and the assumption of unchanged vessel topology during short clips are retained. The added methodological analogies introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: unsupervised video vessel segmentation through test-time training, the XACV dataset, and improved segmentation and generalization with temporal coherence.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 removes the discussion of personalized diagnostics and the assertion that test-time training significantly improves diagnostic accuracy and effectiveness. It adds a connection between dense deformation fields and temporal coherence. The stated preprocessing, runtime, and applicability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, runtime, and access disclosures are retained, including PyTorch/Adam, RTX 4090, batch size 16, 512×512 images, approximately 20-minute processing, and the supplementary code/sample-data description. Appendix D is relabeled Section 9.

R1.justification: v4 adds four references: Narcan, Hybrid Neural Fusion for Full-frame Video Stabilization, Robust Dynamic Radiance Fields, and BoostMVSNeRFs. Sections 3.2–3.3 make limited connections to canonical representations and dense warping; all earlier references and the broader research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in Sections 3.2–3.3, scattered grammatical edits, and new acknowledgements. Appendices A–D become supplementary Sections 6–9 with a Supplementary Material heading. The overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 10 moves from the right column to below Table 2 in the left column. Caption typesetting, text flow, and supplementary title/page formatting also change. The two tables and fifteen figures retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: The added connections in Sections 3.2–3.3 modestly improve research context. Removing the assertion of improved diagnostic accuracy also better aligns the discussion with the reported segmentation evaluations, which do not test diagnostic outcomes. The empirical evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
